name: All-In Cost Review
description: Case-pool variant of Total Cost Breakdown, for Problem Recognition.
formula: Total Cost = Total Variable Cost + Total Fixed Cost
business_contexts: a contract manufacturer combining raw materials spend with plant overhead for the year
a boutique hotel adding up housekeeping supplies alongside its fixed lease payment
a regional airline combining fuel spend with fixed aircraft leasing costs
an e-commerce brand combining packaging spend with fixed warehouse rent
a dental practice combining supply costs with fixed staff salaries
question_patterns: Once every variable and fixed expense is added up, what does the client actually spend to run this operation?
What is the full expense bill the client is carrying, once every cost line is combined?
Adding the pieces below together, what does it cost the client to operate for the period?
What is the client's all-in spend once every cost component shown is combined?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate total cost = total_variable_cost + total_fixed_cost
key_insight: Total cost is a simple sum, but the split between variable and fixed is what actually drives breakeven and margin math downstream.
common_mistakes: Adding only one cost component and forgetting the other
Treating fixed costs as if they scale with volume when they don't
framework_soundbite: Total cost is variable plus fixed — the split matters more than the sum.
